sentences.text: Dakotadon is a genus of iguanodont dinosaur known for its distinctive teeth, which are preserved in a partial skull fossil.
Gregory S. Paul estimated this animal to be 6 meters long with a body mass of 1 metric ton.
Dakotadon is notable for being the most complete Early Cretaceous dinosaur known from the Black Hills region.
Despite sharing unique features with European Iguanodon species, the animal had fewer teeth and other traits suggesting it was more distantly related.

The fossil material was originally found by Louis Rossow in outcrops near Whitewood, South Dakota, and a partial skull and associated skeleton were brought to the attention of John Willard in November 1985.
The specimen was donated to the South Dakota School of Mines and Technology Museum and accessioned as SDSM 8656.
In spring 2014, researchers returned to the original fossil site east of Whitewood, guided by the grandchildren of the original discoverer Louis Rossow.
Dakotadon was first described in 1989 as the species Iguanodon lakotaensis by paleontologists David B. Weishampel and Philip R. Bjork.
Dakotadon belongs to the infraorder Ornithopoda and is classified within the unranked family Iguanodontia.
Gregory S. Paul classified Dakotadon as a basal iguanodont that falls outside the families Iguanodontidae and Iguanodontoidea.
Gregory S. Paul established the genus Dakotadon for I. lakotaensis in 2008.
Dakotadon lived during the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian to Barremian) in the Lakota Formation of South Dakota, USA.
Revised stratigraphic analysis dates Dakotadon to the late Valanginian to early Barremian, an older age than previously thought.
The time range for Dakotadon is estimated to be between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.

The classification of Dakotadon is controversial; while some researchers view it as a distinct basal iguanodont related to Theiophytalia, David Norman has argued it is a synonym of Iguanodon bernissartensis.
